definition_zh: 在周围；大约；到处
definition_en: on every side of something, or about a number, or in many places
core_image: 湖边一圈树把水面围在中间
scene: 湖边一圈都长着树，水面被围在中间。 Trees grow around the lake.
sceneCN: 这里 around 是「在周围」（第 1 个义项：在四周环绕）；句意为湖边四周长着树。

senses.title: On every side
senses.definition: on every side of something, enclosing it
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的四周，把它围住
senses.example: Trees grow around the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 湖边四周长着树。
senses.why: A circle about a centre puts things on every side, which is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 绕中心的一圈把东西放到四面八方，这就是第一义。

senses.title: About a number
senses.definition: about a number or a time, near but not exact
senses.definitionCN: 指数量或时间接近但不精确
senses.example: There were around thirty people.
senses.exampleCN: 大约有三十个人。
senses.why: Moving about a point without fixing it gives the loose sense of about a number.
senses.whyCN: 绕着一点移动而不定死，就得到数量上「大约」的宽松义。

senses.title: In many places
senses.definition: from one place to another without a fixed direction
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定方向地从一处到另一处
senses.example: They walked around the town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在镇上四处走动。
senses.why: The same circling is opened up into roaming, which gives the sense of here and there.
senses.whyCN: 同样的绕圈被展开成游走，于是有「四处」的义项。

definition_en: of high quality, thin or delicate, clear and bright, or satisfactory; as a noun and verb, a sum paid as punishment
core_image: 一根细线在阳光下亮得几乎透明，品质与纤细合为一体
scene: 天气预报刚结束，阳光下孩子们的球赛已经开场。 The morning was fine, so the match went ahead.
sceneCN: 这里 fine 是形容词，指「晴朗的」，对应第 3 个义项；句意为早晨天气晴好，比赛如期进行。

pos.zh: 好的；优质的；晴朗的；纤细的

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: of very good quality or skill
senses.definitionCN: 质量或技艺极佳的
senses.example: The museum holds a fine collection of jade.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏了精美的玉器。
senses.why: What is rare and well made earns praise: quality is the root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 稀少而精良之物值得称赞：品质是这个词的根。

senses.title: Thin and delicate
senses.definition: very thin or in very small pieces
senses.definitionCN: 极细的或被切得极小的
senses.example: The brush drew a fine line.
senses.exampleCN: 画笔勾勒出一条细线。
senses.why: Thin is precious in craft: the finer the line, the finer the hand.
senses.whyCN: 工艺以细为贵：线条越细，手上功夫越精。

senses.title: Clear and cloudless
senses.definition: bright and without rain or clouds
senses.definitionCN: 明亮而无雨无云的
senses.example: We chose a fine day for the picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们挑了个晴天去野餐。
senses.why: Weather without cloud is weather of quality: the same root praises it.
senses.whyCN: 无云的天气就是好天气：同一词根表达赞美。

senses.title: Satisfactory; well
senses.definition: in a good or acceptable state
senses.definitionCN: 处于良好或可接受的状态
senses.example: Everything is fine now.
senses.exampleCN: 现在一切都好了。
senses.why: Acceptable is a soft form of excellent: good enough to pass.
senses.whyCN: 「可以」是「极好」的柔化版本：好到足以过关。

senses.title: Money paid as punishment
senses.definition: a sum of money paid as a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚而缴付的款项
senses.example: He paid a fine for parking.
senses.exampleCN: 他因乱停车缴了罚款。
senses.why: Money settles the score the fist once did: an ending priced in cash.
senses.whyCN: 金钱接替拳头来了结恩怨：一次用现金定价的了结。

intro.en: Fine comes from Latin finis 'an end', for a settled payment, and via Old French for a finished, refined quality.
intro.cn: fine 源自拉丁语 finis「终结」，一脉指已定结的罚金，经古法语另一脉指精炼完备的品质。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary', the root also of final and finish.
items.cn: finis 意为「终结、边界」，也是 final 与 finish 的词根。

items.en: Medieval Latin finis took the sense of 'a payment that settles a dispute'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 finis 衍生出「了结争端的款项」义。

items.en: Old French fin meant both 'settled payment' and 'of refined quality'.
items.cn: 古法语 fin 兼指「已定的款项」与「精炼的品质」。

items.en: Middle English borrowed fine in both directions, quality and penalty.
items.cn: 中古英语沿两条路径借入 fine：品质与罚金。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective rich — fine weather, fine silk — and the fine of law.
items.cn: 现代英语保留丰富的形容词义与法律上的罚款义。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fin- root or close spelling; near-meaning words cover quality and thinness.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fin- 词根或相近拼写；近义组覆盖品质与纤细。

senses.title: A violent outbreak

senses.title: To accuse someone of doing wrong
senses.definition: to officially say that someone has done something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 正式指称某人做了错事或违法行为
senses.example: The police charged him with taking the bike.
senses.exampleCN: 警方指控他拿走了自行车。
senses.why: A charge was also a burden laid on a person, and an accusation loads guilt onto someone like a weight.
senses.whyCN: charge 也指压在人身上的担子，指控就像把罪责这个重物压到人身上。

senses.title: To fill a battery with electricity
senses.definition: to put electricity into a battery or device
senses.definitionCN: 把电输入电池或设备
senses.example: Remember to charge your tablet before class.
senses.exampleCN: 上课前记得给平板电脑充电。
senses.why: Filling a battery is loading power into it, the same picture of putting a load into something.
senses.whyCN: 充电就是把电力「装进」设备，与「把负荷装入某物」是同一画面。

senses.title: To rush forward to attack
senses.definition: to run quickly and directly towards someone or something, especially to attack
senses.definitionCN: 快速径直冲向某人或某物，尤指发起攻击
senses.example: The dog charged at the ball and grabbed it.
senses.exampleCN: 狗朝球猛冲过去，一把叼住。
senses.why: A charge in battle is a loaded rush with all one's force, extending 'load' to 'full-speed attack'.
senses.whyCN: 战场上的冲锋是倾尽全力的突袭，把「装载」延伸为「全速突进」。

senses.title: The duty of looking after someone or something
senses.definition: the responsibility given to someone to control or care for something
senses.definitionCN: 交给某人掌管或照看某事的责任
senses.example: Ms Li is in charge of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 李老师负责管理图书馆。
senses.why: The load handed to a person becomes the responsibility itself, so being in charge is carrying that load.
senses.whyCN: 交付给某人的负荷就成了责任本身，in charge 即挑起这副担子。

senses.title: A price asked for something
senses.definition: an amount of money asked for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 为商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The delivery charge is five yuan.
senses.exampleCN: 送货费是五块钱。
senses.why: The act of asking money turns into the money asked, a normal shift from action to result.
senses.whyCN: 索取金钱的行为转为所索的金额，是常见的由动作转结果。

senses.title: Electric energy stored in a battery or body
senses.definition: the amount of electricity stored or carried by something
senses.definitionCN: 某物储存或携带的电量
senses.example: The battery still has some charge left.
senses.exampleCN: 电池里还剩一点电量。
senses.why: What has been loaded into the battery can be named by the loading word itself.
senses.whyCN: 装入电池的东西，就用「装入」这个词来命名。

intro.en: Charge comes from a Late Latin word for loading a cart or horse, reaching English through Old French.
intro.cn: charge 源自晚期拉丁语中「给车马装货」的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Late Latin carricare meant to load a wheeled vehicle, built on carrus, a cart.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 carricare 指给车装货，源于 carrus（四轮车）。

items.en: Old French chargier meant to load, weigh down or entrust a duty.
items.cn: 古法语 chargier 指装载、压负或托付职责。

items.en: Middle English chargen covered loading, burdening and entrusting responsibilities.
items.cn: 中古英语 chargen 涵装载、负重与托付责任。

items.en: Senses multiplied: prices, accusations, military rushes and duties.
items.cn: 义项倍增：收费、控告、军事冲锋与职责。

items.en: Modern English adds the electrical sense: to charge batteries and speak of electric charge.
items.cn: 现代英语增加电学义：给电池充电、谈论电荷。

scene: 雨夜的街口，反光背心上的徽记在车灯里闪了一下，那人抬手示意车辆慢下来。 A young officer stepped into the road and raised one hand.

senses.title: A commissioned member of the armed forces
senses.definition: a member of the army, navy or air force who holds a rank and gives orders to others
senses.definitionCN: 在陆军、海军或空军中拥有军衔并向他人下达命令的人
senses.example: Her brother is an officer in the navy.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥是海军军官。
senses.why: Officium meant a charge entrusted to someone; an army hands part of its command to named individuals, so the person who holds that charge is called an officer before any uniform is mentioned.
senses.whyCN: officium 指的是托付给某人的职责；军队把一部分指挥权交给具体的人，于是这个承担职责的人先于军装被称为 officer。

senses.title: A member of a police force with authority
senses.definition: a member of a police force, especially one who has the power to direct other constables
senses.definitionCN: 警队成员，尤指有权指挥其他警员的人
senses.example: A police officer asked to see his licence.
senses.exampleCN: 一名警官要求查看他的执照。
senses.why: A police force copies the army's habit of ranking people by the charge they hold, so the same title moves into the body that keeps order in the streets.
senses.whyCN: 警队沿用了军队按职责定级的做法，同一个头衔于是走进维持街头秩序的队伍。

senses.title: An official in a government department or organization
senses.definition: a person who holds a named position of authority in a government department or another organization
senses.definitionCN: 在政府部门或其他机构中担任具名权威职位的人
senses.example: A customs officer checked the bags one by one.
senses.exampleCN: 一名海关官员逐个检查了行李。
senses.why: Any institution that entrusts a task to a named person produces this title, because it marks the charge rather than the uniform of the day.
senses.whyCN: 任何把任务托付给具体个人的机构都会产生这个头衔，因为它标的是职责，而不是当天的制服。

senses.title: A senior member of a company, bank or union
senses.definition: a senior employee of a company, bank or union who is trusted with a particular duty
senses.definitionCN: 公司、银行或工会中被托付某项专门职责的高级雇员
senses.example: The bank officer explained the loan terms.
senses.exampleCN: 银行职员解释了贷款条款。
senses.why: Firms borrowed the word to mark staff who carry a special charge, so a clerk trusted with loans becomes an officer of the bank even without any state authority.
senses.whyCN: 企业借来这个词标注承担专门职责的职员，于是被托付贷款事务的柜员成了银行的 officer，尽管手里并没有国家权力。

intro.en: Officer is the person-shaped form of officium: a duty needs someone to carry it, and that someone took the name of the duty itself.
intro.cn: officer 是 officium 的人形版本：一份职责总要有人来承担，而承担者直接拿走了职责的名字。

items.en: Officium named a service, a duty and later a post held under the Roman state.
items.cn: officium 指服务、职责，后来也指在罗马城邦下担任的职位。

items.en: Officiarius named the person who performed an office or a service, and the suffix marks a holder of some charge.
items.cn: officiarius 指履行职务或服务的人，后缀标出「持有某项职责」的人。

items.en: Old French officier named the man who carried out a charge, whether in a court, in a noble household or in war.
items.cn: 古法语 officier 指执行某项职务的男子，无论在法庭、贵族府邸还是战场上。

items.en: English first used officer for a person holding a charge under a lord or a court, and only later for a commander in the army and navy.
items.cn: 英语最初用 officer 指在领主或法庭之下担职的人，后来才指陆海军的指挥官。

items.en: Modern English spreads the title across police, customs, banks and clubs while keeping the old core of a named charge.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个头衔铺到警队、海关、银行与社团，同时保留了「一份具名职责」的老核心。

note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「职责」之上的同族词；近义组收表示军衔与权威职位的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a duty with a person attached to it: the Latin noun for a charge takes an ending that means the one who holds it.

normal.en: Officer is built on officium, a duty, so the title answers the question of what a person is charged with, not who he is.
normal.cn: officer 建在 officium（职责）之上，所以这个头衔回答的是「他担着什么差事」，而不是「他是什么人」。

normal.en: The ending -er marks the doer, exactly as it does in worker and teacher.
normal.cn: -er 标出做事的人，和 worker、teacher 里的用法完全一样。

normal.en: An army calls a rank a commission, and the holder of a commission is a commissioned officer.
normal.cn: 军队把军衔称作委任，持有委任的人就是 commissioned officer。

normal.en: Customs officer, bank officer and club officer all carry one idea: a named charge inside an institution.
normal.cn: 海关官员、银行职员、社团干事共有一个意思：机构内部一份具名的职责。

normal.en: Police and army share the title because both organize people by the charge each one carries.
normal.cn: 警队与军队共用这个头衔，因为两者都按每人所负的职责来组织人。

abstract.en: The stripe on a sleeve adds no strength; it adds responsibility.

abstract.en: Every officer is a person to whom an institution has handed a piece of its authority.
abstract.cn: 每个官员都是机构把一部分权威交到手里的人。

root: 拉丁语 officium（职责、服务）→ 晚期拉丁语 officiarius（履行职务的人）→ 古法语 officier → 英语 officer；词义始终围绕「被托付一项职责的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person charged with a duty; the senses fan out into the army, the police, government departments and the senior staff of a company.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是承担一份职责的人；义项展开到军队、警队、政府部门，以及企业里的高级职员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single stripe on a sleeve, marking not extra strength but a charge that this person must answer for.
core.cn: 核心意象：袖口上的一道横杠，标的不是多余的力气，而是这个人必须为之负责的一份职责。

branches.en: a naval uniform at a family dinner table
branches.cn: 家宴桌旁的一身海军军装

branches.en: a hand raised to slow traffic on a wet night
branches.cn: 雨夜里抬起手让车慢下来

branches.en: a customs counter piled with opened bags
branches.cn: 海关柜台上摊开的行李

branches.en: a clerk pointing at a line of fine print
branches.cn: 职员指着条款里的一行小字

branches.en: two uniforms that both answer to one title
branches.cn: 两身制服共用一个头衔

intro.en: The word is a Latin duty-noun plus a person-suffix; English then adds endings of its own to name the act and the status.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语职责名词加一个指人的后缀；英语又加上自己的词尾，造出动作与身份。

latinIntro.en: Latin officium and its late form officiarius lead through French officier to the English title, so the whole chain names the holder of a charge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 officium 及其晚期形式 officiarius 经法语 officier 走到英语的这个头衔，整条链都在说「持有职责的人」。

definition_zh: 代表；表示；描绘；相当于
definition_en: to act or speak for someone, to stand for something, or to show something in a picture or description
core_image: 一个人站在一群人前面，把大家的意思带到会议桌上
scene: 村里选出一个人去城里开会，他要代表所有住户表达对修路的需求。 She was chosen to represent the village at the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 represent 是「代表」（第 1 个义项：代替某人或某群体发言、行事）；句意：她被选出来代表全村去开会。

derivatives.zh: 代表；表现；描绘
代表
具象的；表现的

senses.title: To act or speak for others
senses.definition: to act or speak officially for a person, group, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 正式代替某人、某群体或某组织行事或发言
senses.example: The lawyer represents several families in the case.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师在案件中代表好几个家庭。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to make present, so representing is making an absent group present through one person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「使在场」，所以代表就是让不在场的群体通过一个人「到场」。

senses.title: To stand for something
senses.definition: to be a sign or symbol of something
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事物的标志或象征
senses.example: On the map, a red dot represents a hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 在地图上，红点表示医院。
senses.why: A symbol makes an idea present to the eye, which is the same logic as a person standing for a group.
senses.whyCN: 符号让一个概念在眼前「在场」，这与人代表群体的逻辑相同。

senses.title: To show in picture or words
senses.definition: to describe or show something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式描述或呈现某事物
senses.example: The painting represents the harvest as a celebration.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画把丰收描绘成一场庆典。
senses.why: A picture makes a scene present again, extending the core idea from people to images.
senses.whyCN: 图画让一个场景再次「在场」，把核心概念从人扩展到图像。

senses.title: To amount to something
senses.definition: to be equivalent to something, or to count as an example of it
senses.definitionCN: 等同于某事物，或算作某事物的一例
senses.example: The delay represents a serious loss for the company.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对公司来说相当于严重损失。
senses.why: If something stands for a value or result, it can also count as that result in practice.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物代表某种价值或结果，它在实际中也就可以算作那个结果。

intro.en: Represent comes from Latin repraesentare, to make present, built from re- and praesentare, to present.
intro.cn: represent 来自拉丁语 repraesentare（使在场），由 re- 与 praesentare（呈现）构成。

items.en: Praesens means present or being at hand, and praesentare means to make present.
items.cn: praesens 意为在场的、手边的，praesentare 意为使在场。

items.en: Repraesentare adds re- and means to bring something before the eyes or mind.
items.cn: repraesentare 加上 re-，意为把某物带到眼前或心中。

items.en: The verb is used for showing an image, a person, or an idea.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，该动词用于呈现图像、人物或观念。

items.en: Old French representer carries the senses of showing and standing for.
items.cn: 古法语 representer 同时有「展示」和「代表」的意思。

items.en: Middle English represent covers speaking for others and depicting scenes.
items.cn: 中古英语 represent 涵盖替人发言和描绘场景。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of amounting to or constituting something.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「相当于、构成」这一义项。

note.en: Represent is the verb at the centre of a family about standing in for something, and it sits near words for symbol and depiction.
note.cn: represent 是「代替某物出场」这一词族的中心动词，与表示象征和描绘的词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of representing or something that represents
a person chosen to act for others
showing things as they appear in real life
to be a symbol of something
to show something in a picture or description
to give a visible or concrete form to an idea
to be a sign or short form of something

normalIntro.en: Represent is re- plus present, so the memory hook is making something present again through a person, sign, or picture.
normalIntro.cn: represent 就是 re- 加 present，记忆钩子是「通过人、符号或图画让某物再次在场」。

normal.en: Re- means again, and present means here: make the group present again through one speaker.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，present 表示在场：通过一个发言者让群体再次到场。

normal.en: A red dot on a map represents a hospital by making it visible.
normal.cn: 地图上的红点通过「可见」来代表医院。

normal.en: The ending -ation turns the verb into the noun representation.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ation 把动词变成名词 representation。

normal.en: The ending -ative turns it into representative, the person or the adjective.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ative 把它变成 representative，可指人或作形容词。

normal.en: Represent an improvement means the thing amounts to an improvement.
normal.cn: represent an improvement 意为该事物相当于一种改进。

abstract.en: Picture one person carrying a whole village's questions into a meeting room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把整个村子的问题带进会议室。

abstract.en: Imagine a small icon standing in for a large building on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一枚小图标代替一栋大楼。

abstract.en: Think of a portrait making an absent face look present.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像让不在场的面孔重新出现。

examples.en: She represents the company in Asia.
examples.cn: 她代表公司在亚洲开展工作。

examples.en: In this diagram, each circle represents a cell.
examples.cn: 在这张图里，每个圆圈表示一个细胞。

examples.en: The new rules represent a major change.
examples.cn: 新规定相当于一次重大变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（再次）+ present（呈现）＝让不在场的人或事再次呈现，即代表；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ praesens（在场的）→ praesentare（使在场）→ repraesentare（呈现、代表）→ 古法语 representer → 中古英语 represent。

sensesIntro.en: Making something present is the core: a person makes a group present, a sign makes an idea present, a picture makes a scene present, and a fact can make a result present.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使某物在场」：人让群体在场，符号让观念在场，图画让场景在场，而事实可以让结果在场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person or sign standing in so that something absent becomes present.
core.cn: 核心意象：由一个人或符号代替出场，使缺席之物重新在场。

branches.en: Acting for a group is the central political and legal sense.
branches.cn: 替群体行事，是最核心的政治与法律义项。

branches.en: A symbol makes an idea present to the eye.
branches.cn: 符号让观念在眼前呈现。

branches.en: A picture makes a scene present again in description.
branches.cn: 图画在描述中让场景再次呈现。

branches.en: A fact can make a consequence present by counting as it.
branches.cn: 事实可以通过「算作」某种后果而使之在场。

branches.en: Delegates and symbols both stand in for something larger.
branches.cn: 代表与符号都在代替更大的事物出场。

intro.en: Represent is built from Latin parts, and its English family grows through noun and adjective endings.
intro.cn: represent 由拉丁语成分构成，其英语词族通过名词和形容词词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- adds again, and praesentare means to make present, from praesens, present.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 增添「再次」，praesentare 意为「使在场」，来自 praesens（在场的）。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 represent 与 present 开头。

items.example: Praesens is the source of the present element.
items.exampleCN: praesens 是 present 这一成分的来源。

items.example: Praesentare gives represent its showing sense.
items.exampleCN: praesentare 给 represent 提供「呈现」的含义。
repraesentare 由 re- 与 praesentare 合成。

items.example: Represent carries the Latin verb into English.
items.exampleCN: represent 把拉丁动词带入英语。

items.meaning: the act or result of representing

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

definition_zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价；提议；报价；特价
definition_en: to give or present something to someone; to say you are willing to do something; to name a price; as a noun, a proposal, a bid or a special deal
core_image: 双手把东西捧到别人面前，等对方伸手接下
scene: 公交车上人挨着人，一位老人扶着扶手晃了一下，靠窗的年轻人抬手指了指自己旁边的空位。 She offered her seat to the old man and he took it with a nod.
sceneCN: 这里 offer 是「提供、让出」（第 1 个义项：把东西给予别人）；句意是她把座位让给了老人，老人点头接受。画面里有拥挤的车厢和一个靠窗的空位。

pos.zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价
提议；报价；录用通知；特价

derivatives.zh: 由 offer 加 -ing 构成，义为「献上的东西；祭品；提供的服务或课程」
法律用语，由 offer 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「提出要约的一方」
源自拉丁 offertorium，与 offer 同一词根，义为「礼拜中的奉献环节或奉献金」

senses.title: To give or present something to someone
senses.definition: to give something to someone, especially in a polite or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指以礼貌或正式的方式把某物给予别人
senses.example: She offered him a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她给他端来一杯茶。
senses.why: Latin offerre meant to bring something before a person, and that picture of presenting an object still drives the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offerre 意为把东西带到某人面前，这幅「捧到人前」的画面一直支撑着第一个义项。

senses.title: To say that you are willing to do something
senses.definition: to express willingness to do something for someone
senses.definitionCN: 向别人表示自己愿意做某事
senses.example: He offered to drive us to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。
senses.why: Once the thing brought forward can be an action rather than an object, the verb comes to mean putting yourself forward as willing.
senses.whyCN: 当被捧到人前的不再是物件而是一个行动，这个动词就引申为「把自己递上去」，表示愿意效劳。

senses.title: To name a price for something
senses.definition: to say what price you will pay for something or charge for it
senses.definitionCN: 说出你愿意为某物支付、或为某物开出的价钱
senses.example: They offered two million for the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出价两百万买那栋房子。
senses.why: In a market the thing brought forward is a sum of money, so presenting turns into bidding.
senses.whyCN: 在市场里，被捧到人前的变成一笔钱，于是「呈上」就转成了「出价」。

senses.title: A proposal or a job offer
senses.definition: a formal proposal, especially one made to be accepted or refused
senses.definitionCN: 正式的提议，尤指摆出来等对方接受或拒绝的那种
senses.example: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。
senses.why: The noun keeps the object that was brought forward, so an offer is the proposal itself, waiting for a yes or a no.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了那个被捧出来的东西，所以 an offer 就是摆在面前、等人点头或摇头的提议。

senses.title: A special price or deal
senses.definition: a reduced price or a deal advertised to attract buyers
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引买家而宣传的降价价格或优惠方案
senses.example: The shop has a special offer on coffee this week.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店本周咖啡有特价。
senses.why: When a price is put in front of a buyer as a bargain, the same noun narrows to the attractive deal on the label.
senses.whyCN: 当价格作为便宜货摆到买家面前，同一个名词就收窄为标签上那个吸引人的优惠。

intro.en: Offer goes back to a Latin verb meaning to bring before, was borrowed early into Old English for sacrifice, and was then widened by French to any kind of presenting.
intro.cn: offer 可追到拉丁语中意为「带到面前」的动词，早期借入古英语时指献祭，后经法语扩展为一切形式的呈上。

items.en: Offerre joined ob-, meaning toward or before, with ferre, meaning to bring, so it meant to bring something before someone.
items.cn: offerre 把表示「向前、对着」的 ob- 与表示「带来、搬运」的 ferre 合在一起，意为把东西带到某人面前。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin verb early as offrian, and its first use was bringing a sacrifice before God.
items.cn: 古英语早期就把这个拉丁动词借进来写作 offrian，最初用于把祭品献到神面前。

items.en: Norman French offrir reinforced the word and widened it from sacrifice to any act of presenting.
items.cn: 诺曼法语 offrir 重新加固了这个词，并把「献祭」扩展为任何形式的呈上。

items.en: Middle English offer covered presenting gifts, making a proposal and naming a price.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offer 已覆盖呈上礼物、提出建议与开出价钱。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious echo in offering and offertory, and the commercial sense in bid and special offer.
items.cn: 现代英语在 offering 与 offertory 里保留宗教余音，在出价与特价里保留商业含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derivatives and other words built on the Latin verb for carrying; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving, proposing and bidding.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同样建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上的词；近义组收表示给予、提议与出价的动词。

entries.definition: Something presented, especially to a god or to a fund.
entries.definitionCN: 献上的东西，尤指献神或捐献之物。

entries.definition: The part of a church service when gifts are collected.
entries.definitionCN: 礼拜中收集奉献的环节。

entries.definition: To send a matter or a person to another source, built on the Latin verb for carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 把事务或人转到另一处，建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上。

entries.definition: To move something from one place to another, with the same carrying root.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一处移到另一处，共享同一个「搬运」词根。

entries.definition: To give or hand something to someone, often formally.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物给予或递交某人，常用于正式场合。

entries.definition: To suggest a plan or an idea for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 提出计划或想法供他人考虑。

entries.definition: An offer of a particular amount of money for something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某物开出的某个数目的价钱。

entries.definition: To give someone something they need.
entries.definitionCN: 给某人提供其需要的东西。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for bringing something forward, and its family keeps the picture of a gift placed in front of another person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「把东西向前带」的动词上，同族词始终保留「把礼物摆到别人面前」的画面。

normal.en: Offerre is ob- plus ferre, so the word pictures someone bringing an object forward into view.
normal.cn: offerre 是 ob- 加 ferre，画面就是有人把东西向前带到别人眼前。

normal.en: Old English offrian first meant to sacrifice, which is why offering still sounds religious.
normal.cn: 古英语 offrian 最初指献祭，所以 offering 至今还带宗教味道。

normal.en: Offering adds -ing to offer and names the thing that was placed before someone.
normal.cn: offering 在 offer 后加 -ing，指那个被摆到人前的东西。

normal.en: Offer to do takes an infinitive and marks willingness rather than an object.
normal.cn: offer to do 后面接不定式，标出的是意愿，而不是一件物件。

normal.en: On offer is the British phrase for goods that are available or reduced in price.
normal.cn: on offer 是英式说法，指商品可买到或正在减价。

abstract.en: Picture both hands holding something out at arm's length, waiting for the other person to reach back.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把东西捧出一臂远，等着对方也伸出手来。

abstract.en: A bid is money pushed onto the table, and the other side still has to nod.
abstract.cn: 出价就是把钱推到桌面上，另一头还得点头才行。

abstract.en: Offering help means extending a hand before anyone asks for it.
abstract.cn: 主动帮忙，就是在别人开口之前先把手伸出去。

examples.en: She offered her seat to the old man.
examples.cn: 她把座位让给了那位老人。

examples.en: He offered to drive us to the station.
examples.cn: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。

examples.en: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
examples.cn: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，发了」——哦，发了笔财，是因为有人给你出了个好价；offer 就是提供与出价。

root: 拉丁语 offerre（带到面前）由 ob-（向前、对着）加 ferre（带来、搬运）构成，古英语早期借入作 offrian 表示献祭，又经古法语 offrir 加固；同族词有 offering、offertory。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bringing something before a person; the senses divide into giving, volunteering, naming a price, a proposal and a bargain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把东西带到人面前」；义项分为给予、主动提出、出价、提议与优惠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding an object out towards another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一件东西捧向另一个人。

branches.en: a cup of tea pushed gently across the table
branches.cn: 一杯茶被轻轻推到桌子对面

branches.en: a man saying he will drive everyone home
branches.cn: 一个人说愿意开车送大家回家

branches.en: a price written on a card beside a house
branches.cn: 房子旁卡片上写着一个价格

branches.en: a proposal and a letter of employment laid on a desk
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的提案与录用信

branches.en: a bright label in a shop window
branches.cn: 商店橱窗里醒目的标签

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin prefix of direction, the Latin verb for carrying, the compound they form, and English suffixes for the act and the thing offered.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示方向的拉丁前缀、表示搬运的拉丁动词、二者构成的复合动词，以及分别指「动作」和「所献之物」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the collecting of gifts in a service
place or thing connected with an action
items.meaningCN: 与某动作有关的场所或事物

definition_zh: 九十；九十年代；九十多岁
definition_en: the number equal to nine times ten; also the years of a decade numbered ninety to ninety-nine, and ages in that range
core_image: 摊主把硬币十个一摞码成九摞，最后一摞刚好压到旧布的边缘
scene: 清晨的旧货市场里，摊主把硬币十个一摞码成九摞，最后一摞正好压到旧布的边缘。 The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.
sceneCN: 这里是「九十」这个数目（第 1 个义项：九乘十）；句意为那座旧钟走了九十年仍在计时。图中可辨识物件：硬币摞、旧布边、旧钟。

derivatives.zh: 由 ninety 加序数词尾 -th（拼作 -tieth）构成，义为「第九十」
由 ninety 与 odd 复合构成，义为「九十好几的」

senses.title: The number nine times ten
senses.definition: the number equal to nine groups of ten, written with the digits nine and zero
senses.definitionCN: 等于九组十的数，写作九与零
senses.example: The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟走了九十年仍在计时。
senses.why: Ninety is a native Germanic tens word: nine plus an ending that means a group of ten, so the word itself says nine tens rather than naming a new quantity.
senses.whyCN: ninety 是日耳曼语本土的十位词：九加上表示「一组十」的词尾，所以这个词自己就在说「九个十」，而不是给一个新数量另起名字。

senses.title: The decade numbered ninety to ninety-nine
senses.definition: the period of ten years in a century numbered from ninety to ninety-nine, usually written the nineties
senses.definitionCN: 一个世纪里编号从九十到九十九的那十年，通常写作 the nineties
senses.example: The building was put up in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼建于九十年代。
senses.why: A century is a run of hundred years, so the last ten can be named by the tens word that opens them; English uses the plural to mean the whole span, not one year.
senses.whyCN: 一个世纪是一百年的长串，最后十年可以用开启它的那个十位数来命名；英语用复数表示整段，而不是单独一年。

senses.title: An age between ninety and ninety-nine
senses.definition: the ages from ninety to ninety-nine, especially in the phrase in one's nineties
senses.definitionCN: 从九十岁到九十九岁之间的年龄，尤用于 in one's nineties 这一说法
senses.example: She is still writing in her nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她九十多岁仍在写作。
senses.why: An age range is also a span of ten, so the same plural serves for a person's tenth decade; being in the nineties means living inside that stretch.
senses.whyCN: 年龄区间同样是一段十岁，于是同一个复数也用来指人生的第十个十年；in one's nineties 就是活在那一段里。

intro.en: Ninety is one of the native tens numerals English builds by joining a unit to an ending for a group of ten, and its plural later took on the meaning of a decade.
intro.cn: ninety 是英语本土的十位数之一，由个位数加表示「一组十」的词尾拼成；它的复数后来又承担了「十年」的意思。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants, and the exact shape of that base is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构的，这个底座的确切形状存疑。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine and the base of both the tens numeral and the ordinal.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是这个十位数与对应序数词的共同底座。

items.en: The ending -tig meant a group of ten, so nigontig said nine tens in one word.
items.cn: 词尾 -tig 表示「一组十」，因此 nigontig 用一个词说出九个十。

items.en: Middle English kept the tens numeral as nineti and used the plural for groups and repeated counts.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个十位数保留为 nineti，并用复数表示多组或反复计数。

items.en: Modern English uses ninety as a number and the nineties for a decade, an age range and temperatures near ninety.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ninety 表示数目，用 the nineties 表示十年、年龄区间以及九十度上下的温度。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps to words built on the same nine base; the near-meaning group puts ninety on the same number line as its neighbours and the ten-year span it names.
note.cn: 形近组只收建在同一个「九」底座上的词；近义组把 ninety 放回同一条数轴，与相邻的数以及它所代表的那段十年对照。

entries.definition: A period of ten years, the unit that makes the nineties a span.

normalIntro.en: The word is nine plus an old ending for a group of ten, and its plural extends the number into a decade and a decade of a life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「九」加上一个表示「一组十」的古老词尾，它的复数形式又把数目伸向十年和人生的十年。

normal.en: Ninety is nine tens: nine plus the -ty ending, which came from an Old English word for a group of ten.
normal.cn: 九十就是九个十：九加上 -ty 词尾，这个词尾来自古英语里表示「一组十」的词。

normal.en: The same base gives nineteen with -teen and ninety with -ty, so the two endings tell you whether ten is added or multiplied.
normal.cn: 同一个底座加上 -teen 得到 nineteen，加上 -ty 得到 ninety，两个词尾告诉你十是被加还是被乘。

normal.en: Ninetieth is ninety plus -th, the ordinary way English turns a count into a rank.
normal.cn: ninetieth 是 ninety 加 -th，正是英语把计数变成名次的寻常做法。

normal.en: The plural nineties names both a decade and an age range, because each is a block of ten years.
normal.cn: 复数 nineties 既指一个年代，也指一个年龄段，因为两者都是一块十年的长度。

normal.en: Ninety-nine is the last number before the next hundred, so ninety sits at the top of the two-digit tens.
normal.cn: 九十九是下一个百之前的最后一个数，所以九十站在两位数十位数的顶端。

abstract.en: A number made by stacking nine groups of ten carries its own explanation inside it, which is why tens words feel so transparent.
abstract.cn: 一个由九个十堆起来的数，把自己的解释藏在词里，所以十位词读起来总显得透明。

abstract.en: The jump from number to decade costs no new word, because a decade is simply ten counted one after another.
abstract.cn: 从数目跳到年代不需要另造新词，因为一整个年代不过是把十一个个数下去。

abstract.en: Ninety marks the last stretch before a hundred, the point where counting starts to feel like a rounder kind of arithmetic.
abstract.cn: 九十标出百之前的最后一段，正是计数开始变得像整块算术的地方。

normalIntro.en: Salt is the white seasoning that makes food taste savoury.
normalIntro.cn: salt 是让食物有咸味的白色调味品。

normal.en: Add a pinch of salt to the soup.
normal.cn: 往汤里加一小撮盐。

normal.en: Sea salt is coarser than table salt.
normal.cn: 海盐比食盐颗粒更粗。

normal.en: He salted the meat to keep it fresh.
normal.cn: 他用盐腌肉以保鲜。

normal.en: Too much salt is bad for your blood pressure.
normal.cn: 盐吃太多对血压不好。

normal.en: Take his advice with a grain of salt.
normal.cn: 对他的建议要打个折扣。

abstract.en: Picture white crystals falling onto a hot dish.
abstract.cn: 想象白色晶体落在热菜上。

abstract.en: Imagine the sea leaving salt on the rocks.
abstract.cn: 想象海水在岩石上留下盐。

abstract.en: Think of salt as a tiny key that unlocks flavour.
abstract.cn: 把盐想成一把释放味道的小钥匙。

examples.en: The recipe calls for a teaspoon of salt.
examples.cn: 这个食谱需要一茶匙盐。

examples.en: Salt was once used as money in some cultures.
examples.cn: 在某些文化中盐曾被当作货币。

examples.en: She salted the pasta water generously.
examples.cn: 她在煮意面的水里放了充足的盐。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁词根
dict_mnemonic.text: salt 与拉丁语 sal（盐）同源，salary（薪水）原指发给士兵买盐的钱。

root: salt 源自古英语 sealt，与拉丁语 sal（盐）同源；英语 salary 也与「盐」的历史有关。

sensesIntro.en: Salt is the seasoning, a class of chemical compounds, or the act of adding it to food.
sensesIntro.cn: salt 指调味盐、化学盐类，或给食物加盐的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white crystals that change how food tastes.
core.cn: 核心意象：改变食物味道的白色晶体。

branches.en: The base sense is the seasoning on the table.
branches.cn: 基础义是餐桌上的调味盐。

branches.en: Chemistry extends the name to acid-base compounds.
branches.cn: 化学把这名称扩展到酸碱化合物。

branches.en: The verb applies the seasoning to food.
branches.cn: 动词义把调味盐用到食物上。

branches.en: Common salt is one chemical salt among many.
branches.cn: 食盐只是众多化学盐类之一。

branches.en: Seasoning and salting describe the same kitchen action.
branches.cn: 调味与加盐描述同一个厨房动作。

intro.en: Salt is a short native root that builds several everyday words.
intro.cn: salt 是一个简短的本族词根，能构成多个日常词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin sal, salis, and salare explain the word family behind salt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sal、salis 与 salare 解释了 salt 背后的词族。

items.example: Mineral salts occur in the soil.
The saltiness of the cheese surprised me.
items.exampleCN: 这奶酪的咸度让我惊讶。
海水鱼需要特殊的水族箱。

items.meaning: a small container for table salt
a place where salt is dug out
items.example: They toured an old salt mine.
items.exampleCN: 他们参观了一座旧盐矿。

items.meaning: low coastal land often covered by seawater
items.example: Birds nest in the salt marsh.

latinEntries.example: Sal is the Latin word for salt.
Salis shows the stem used in compounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: salis 展示了复合词中使用的词干。

latinEntries.example: Salare means to treat with salt.

definition_zh: 笑话；玩笑；笑料；开玩笑道；开玩笑的对象
definition_en: something said or done to make people laugh, or a person or thing that invites teasing
core_image: 一桌人听到一句话后同时笑出声，杯子都晃了一下
scene: 晚饭后客厅里坐满亲戚，舅舅讲起年轻时的糗事。 His story about the broken chair got the biggest joke of the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 joke 是「笑话」（第 1 个义项：引人发笑的话或事），句意为他把那把坏椅子的糗事讲得成了当晚最大的笑料。画面里的物件：客厅、沙发、茶杯。

pos.zh: 名词：笑话；玩笑；笑料；笑柄

derivatives.zh: 由 joke 加 -er 构成，义为「爱开玩笑的人；扑克里的大王」
由 joke 加 -ing 构成，义为「开玩笑的」
由 joking 加 -ly 构成，义为「开玩笑地」
由 joke 加 -y 构成，义为「爱打趣的；轻松逗趣的」

senses.title: Something said to make people laugh
senses.definition: a short story or remark with a funny turn that makes people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 带有出人意料的滑稽转折，使人发笑的话或短故事
senses.example: He told a joke about two penguins on a bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了个关于两只企鹅坐公交的笑话。
senses.why: The core sense is a spoken turn that produces laughter.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个说出后引来笑声的转折。

senses.title: A playful act or trick
senses.definition: a playful act, often at somebody else's expense
senses.definitionCN: 一种戏耍的举动，常以别人为对象
senses.example: Hiding his shoes was meant as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 把他的鞋藏起来原本是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word widens from a spoken thing to a done thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从说出来的东西扩大到做出来的东西。

senses.title: A mocking remark
senses.definition: a remark made lightly to tease or mock someone
senses.definitionCN: 轻描淡写地用来取笑或挖苦某人的话
senses.example: The boys made jokes about his new haircut.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们拿他的新发型说笑。
senses.why: Laughter can be turned on a person, and the same noun follows.
senses.whyCN: 笑声可以转向某个人，同一个名词也跟着转。

senses.title: A person or thing that invites teasing
senses.definition: a person, plan, or object that seems ridiculous to others
senses.definitionCN: 被别人看作可笑的人、计划或东西
senses.example: The new rule became the joke of the whole office.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定成了整个办公室的笑柄。
senses.why: When the funny thing is the target itself, the noun becomes a label for it.
senses.whyCN: 当可笑的对象本身就是目标时，这个名词就变成给它的标签。

senses.title: To speak or act playfully
senses.definition: to say or do something in play, expecting no serious answer
senses.definitionCN: 带着玩闹意味说话或行事，不指望当真回应
senses.example: I was only joking about the price.
senses.exampleCN: 我不过是拿价格开玩笑。
senses.why: The verb keeps the light, half-serious tone of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了名词那半真半假、轻松的语气。

senses.title: Hard to take seriously
senses.definition: used to say that something is so easy or small it is not worth calling a task
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示某事太容易、太微小，不值得称作难题
senses.example: Fixing that is no joke for a beginner.
senses.exampleCN: 对新手来说，修好那东西可不是说说而已。
senses.why: The idiomatic use keeps the word for things that look light but turn heavy.
senses.whyCN: 这个习语义保留了对「看着轻、其实重」的事物使用该词。

intro.en: Joke came from Latin jocus, a jest, through Italian and French before it reached English.
intro.cn: joke 源于拉丁语 jocus「玩笑」，经由意大利语和法语才进入英语。

items.en: jocus meant a jest, a joke, or a playful word.
items.cn: jocus 意为玩笑、笑话或打趣的话。

items.en: Italian gioco carried the sense of play or sport.
items.cn: 意大利语 gioco 带着「游戏、玩」的意思。

items.en: French jocque named a light saying, and English met the word there.
items.cn: 法语 jocque 指轻松的话，英语是在这里遇到这个词的。

items.en: Joke entered English in the seventeenth century as a noun.
items.cn: joke 在十七世纪作为名词进入英语。

items.en: The verb and the phrase no joke followed within a century.
items.cn: 动词用法与 no joke 的说法在一个世纪内跟上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the joke family; the near-meaning group holds other kinds of fun and laughter.
note.cn: 形近组共用 joke 这一族词；近义组收其他表示玩笑与好笑事物的词。

entries.definition: Someone who jokes, or the highest card in a pack.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joke 加 -er 构成，指爱开玩笑的人或扑克大王。

entries.definition: In a joking manner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 joke 派生，义为「开玩笑地」。

entries.definition: Formal word for playful and humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 同源于拉丁 jocus，较正式的「诙谐的」。

entries.definition: A joke, often in older writing.
entries.definitionCN: 较文雅的说法，义为「玩笑」，多见于旧文字。

entries.definition: A practical joke played on someone.
A short joke, often written for a performer.
entries.definitionCN: 口语里指短小的笑话段子。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the Latin jest to the phrase no joke.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拉丁语的「玩笑」走到 no joke 这种说法。

normal.en: Latin jocus is also the source of jocose.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 jocus 也是 jocose 的来源。

normal.en: Tell a joke is the standard verb pair.
normal.cn: tell a joke 是最标准的动词搭配。

normal.en: Play a joke on someone means the target is a person.
normal.cn: play a joke on someone 指被开玩笑的是人。

normal.en: A practical joke is done rather than told.
normal.cn: practical joke 是做出来的，不是讲出来的。

normal.en: No joke means something is serious after all.
normal.cn: no joke 表示某事其实很严重。

abstract.en: A joke is a small trap set for laughter.
abstract.cn: 笑话是给笑声设的小陷阱。

abstract.en: The same word can be the laughter and the one laughed at.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可以是笑声，也可以是被笑的人。

abstract.en: A joke dies the moment it is explained.
abstract.cn: 笑话一解释就死了。

examples.en: She told a joke that made everyone laugh.
examples.cn: 她讲了个让大家发笑的笑话。

examples.en: They joked about the endless rain all week.
examples.cn: 他们整周都拿下不完的雨开玩笑。

examples.en: Nobody could take his excuse as a joke.
examples.cn: 没人能把他的借口当成玩笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揍客」—— 玩笑开过头，客人就想揍人

root: 拉丁语 jocus「玩笑、戏谑」→ 意大利语 gioco → 法语 jocque → 英语 joke；同族还有 jocose、jocular。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses: a funny story, a playful act, a mocking remark, the laughing stock, the verb, and the ironic phrase no joke.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项：笑话、玩笑举动、取笑的话、笑柄、开玩笑的动词义，以及 no joke 这一反讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken turn that ends in a room full of laughter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话的转折让满屋子人笑出声。

branches.en: THE DINNER TABLE: a story with a funny ending.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：有滑稽结尾的故事。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN SHOES: a trick done rather than told.
branches.cn: 藏起的鞋这条线：做出来而不是讲出来的玩笑。

branches.en: THE SCHOOLYARD: laughter aimed at a person.
branches.cn: 校园这条线：笑声对准了某个人。

branches.en: THE NOTICE BOARD: a rule that everyone ridicules.
branches.cn: 公告板这条线：被所有人嘲笑的规定。

branches.en: THE HALF-SERIOUS VOICE: the joking verb and the phrase about weight.
branches.cn: 半真半假的口气：开玩笑的动词义与表示分量的说法。

intro.en: Joke takes only English endings; the Latin joc- stem shows up in its formal cousins.
intro.cn: joke 只加英语词尾，拉丁 joc- 词干出现在它较正式的亲属词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin relatives descend from jocus, a jest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同族词源自 jocus「玩笑」。

items.exampleCN: no joke 意为非同小可。

definition_zh: 鼓；鼓状物；敲鼓；有节奏地敲击
definition_en: a round musical instrument that you hit, or the container shaped like it
core_image: 蒙着皮的圆筒，被手掌敲响
scene: 节日广场上，一位老艺人把兽皮绷紧在圆筒上。 The old man beat the drum so the whole square could hear.
sceneCN: 这里 drum 是「鼓」（第 1 个义项：敲击发声的圆筒乐器）；句意：老人敲鼓，让整个广场都能听见。

derivatives.zh: drum 加表示者的后缀 er 构成，义为「鼓手」
drum 加 beat 构成，义为「鼓点；鼓声」

senses.title: A percussion instrument
senses.definition: a round instrument with a skin top that makes sound when hit
senses.definitionCN: 顶部蒙皮、敲击发声的圆形乐器
senses.example: The drum kept the beat for the dancers.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓为舞者打着节拍。
senses.why: The instrument is a stretched skin over a hollow round body.
senses.whyCN: 这种乐器是空心圆筒上绷紧的一张皮。

senses.title: A round container
senses.definition: a large round metal container for oil or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 盛放油类或化学品的大型圆金属桶
senses.example: An oil drum stood by the shed.
senses.exampleCN: 棚边立着一只油桶。
senses.why: The round shape of the instrument names any similar round box.
senses.whyCN: 乐器的圆筒外形被借来指任何相似的圆桶。

senses.title: Beat rhythmically
senses.definition: to hit a surface again and again with rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 有节奏地反复敲打某个表面
senses.example: He drummed his fingers on the desk while waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 他等待时用手指在桌上敲个不停。
senses.why: The action of hitting the drum becomes hitting anything in rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 敲鼓的动作泛化为有节奏地敲任何东西。

senses.title: Beat into the mind
senses.definition: to make someone learn something by repeating it again and again
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复重复使某人学会某事
senses.example: Mother drummed good manners into us.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲反复给我们灌输礼貌规矩。
senses.why: Repeated drumbeats fix a rhythm; repeated words fix an idea.
senses.whyCN: 反复的鼓点固定节奏，反复的话语固定观念。

intro.en: Drum is a short word whose history is surprisingly unclear for such an old instrument.
intro.cn: drum 拼写极短，但这件古老乐器的词源却出人意料地不确定。

items.en: Middle English had drom and drumme from the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪起，中古英语出现了 drom 与 drumme。

items.en: One strong theory links it to Dutch trom, the drum, related to trommel.
items.cn: 一种有力的假说把它与荷兰语 trom（鼓，与 trommel 相关）联系起来。

items.en: The sound is imitative of beating, fitting a Germanic echoic origin.
items.cn: 其发音拟声敲击，符合日耳曼拟声起源。

items.en: The exact source is uncertain; the imitative theory and the Dutch theory both lack full proof.
items.cn: 确切来源不确定；拟声说与荷兰语说均无完整证据。

items.en: Modern English settled drum as both instrument and verb, adding barrels and drums of oil.
items.cn: 现代英语把 drum 定型为乐器与动词，又引申出桶装与油桶。

note.en: These words stand near drum in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 drum 相邻。

entries.definition: a person who plays the drum
to take in liquid, different root
the sound or pattern of drum strokes
to strike again and again
a large round container
to hit lightly and quickly

normalIntro.en: Use the skin-over-barrel picture and the drum family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「皮绷圆桶」的画面和 drum 词族来记。

normal.en: play the drum is the first image: skin over a round box.
normal.cn: play the drum 是第一画面：圆箱上蒙皮。

normal.en: drummer is drum plus er, the person behind the beat.
normal.cn: drummer 是 drum 加 er，敲出节奏的人。

normal.en: an oil drum borrows the round shape, not the music.
normal.cn: oil drum 借的是圆筒外形，不是音乐。

normal.en: drum up support sounds like beating a drum to gather people.
normal.cn: drum up support 像敲鼓召集人群。

normal.en: Past tense doubles the m: drummed.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写 m：drummed。

abstract.en: Hear the boom of a big drum roll through a parade.
abstract.cn: 听大鼓的轰鸣滚过游行队伍。

abstract.en: Feel your fingers tapping a desk like tiny sticks.
abstract.cn: 感受手指像小鼓槌一样敲击桌面。

abstract.en: See a lesson repeated until it beats into memory.
abstract.cn: 看一门功课被反复敲打，直到敲进记忆。

examples.en: She joined the band and played the drum at every show.
examples.cn: 她加入乐队，每场演出都打鼓。

examples.en: Rain drummed softly on the tin roof.
examples.cn: 雨点轻轻敲打着铁皮屋顶。

examples.en: The workers rolled an empty drum across the yard.
examples.cn: 工人们把空油桶滚过院子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「咚」——鼓声本来就是「咚咚」响，drum 一念就想起鼓

root: 一般认为拟声词，模拟敲鼓声；一说源自荷兰语 trom、与 trommel（小鼓）相关；确切来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Drum is the beaten round instrument, then its shape in barrels and its rhythm in hands and minds.
sensesIntro.cn: drum 先是被敲的圆乐器，再借外形指圆桶，又借节奏指敲击与灌输。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretched skin that answers every blow
core.cn: 核心意象：一张敲一下就回响的绷紧的皮

branches.en: The instrument with a skin top
branches.cn: 顶部蒙皮的乐器

branches.en: The round barrel of oil
branches.cn: 圆筒形的油桶

branches.en: The fingers tapping in rhythm
branches.cn: 按节奏敲击的手指

branches.en: The lesson repeated like beats
branches.cn: 像鼓点般重复的功课

branches.en: Sound made by repeated striking
branches.cn: 反复敲击发出的声音

intro.en: Drum builds a small family of drummers, beats and barrels.
intro.cn: drum 构成鼓手、鼓点、圆桶等一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Drum is Germanic or imitative in origin, so it has no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: drum 源自日耳曼语或拟声，因此没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a stroke or pattern of drum sounds
a stick for beating a drum
the skin inside the ear that shakes

latinEntries.meaning: a drum, used for the eardrum

definition_zh: 诡计；把戏；窍门；戏弄；哄骗
definition_en: a clever act meant to deceive or amuse someone, or to deceive a person in that way
core_image: 一只手把硬币从这个人眼前晃过，却从那人耳后取出
scene: 街头围了一圈人，那个戴帽子的男人把手绢一晃，鸽子从袖口飞了出来。 He knows a trick that makes a coin disappear.
sceneCN: 这里 trick 是「戏法、把戏」（第 2 个义项：逗人一乐的巧妙手法）；句意为他会一个让硬币消失的戏法。手一晃、东西换个地方出现，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -y 构成形容词，义为「棘手的；狡猾的」
名词加 -ery 构成，义为「欺骗行径」
名词加 -ster 构成，义为「骗子；恶作剧者」

senses.title: A plan to deceive someone
senses.definition: a clever but dishonest plan to get something from someone
senses.definitionCN: 巧妙却不老实、想从别人那里得利的计谋
senses.example: It was a trick to make him sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个骗他签字的诡计。
senses.why: The word comes from Old French trickier, to deceive, and its oldest sense is a cheat or a deceit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古法语 trickier（欺骗），最早的义项就是骗人或骗术。

senses.title: A clever act that amuses
senses.definition: a skilful performance, such as a card trick, done to entertain
senses.definitionCN: 为逗乐而做的熟练表演，如纸牌戏法
senses.example: The children loved the card trick.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们很喜欢那个纸牌戏法。
senses.why: A cheat and a magic show differ only in intent: both turn on a hidden method.
senses.whyCN: 骗人的手法与魔术表演只差用心：两者都靠一套藏着的方法。

senses.title: A clever way of doing something
senses.definition: a special way of doing a task that makes it easier
senses.definitionCN: 让事情变容易的特殊做法
senses.example: The trick is to stir the sauce slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 窍门是慢慢地搅酱汁。
senses.why: The hidden method that deceived someone can also simply help: then we call it the trick.
senses.whyCN: 那套藏着的方法如果不为骗人而是帮忙，我们就叫它窍门。

senses.title: To deceive someone
senses.definition: to make someone believe something untrue so that you gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信不实之事以取得好处
senses.example: They tricked him out of his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们骗走了他的存款。
senses.why: The verb is the act behind the noun: to work the hidden method on a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词背后的动作：把藏着的方法用在某个人身上。

senses.title: A habit or mannerism

intro.en: The word comes from Old French trique, a deceit or a cheat, and the verb trickier, to deceive.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 trique（欺骗、诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗）。

items.en: Trique means a deceit, a shift, or a cheating play, and is used of dice and dealings.
items.cn: 古法语 trique 意为诈术、花招、骗人的把戏，用于骰子与交易。

items.en: English borrows the noun in the fifteenth century for a deceitful act.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，指欺诈行为。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word covers harmless sleight of hand and card play.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已涵盖无害的手法与纸牌戏法。

items.en: Later it names the clever knack of a trade and the odd habit of a person.
items.cn: 后来又用来指行业的技巧与一个人的怪癖。

items.en: The ultimate origin is uncertain; the word may be related to Old French trichier, to cheat.
items.cn: 最终来源不确定；可能和古法语 trichier（欺骗）有关。

definition_zh: 话题；题目；主题；议题
definition_en: the subject of a talk, a piece of writing, or a discussion
core_image: 黑板正中写着一行大字，全班的讨论都围绕它展开
scene: 会议白板上只写了一句话，其余地方都空着，主持人指着它让大家发言。 The topic for today's seminar is how cities treat their rivers.
sceneCN: 这里 topic 是讨论的「主题」（第 1 个义项：谈话或写作的主题）；句意为今天研讨会的主题是城市如何对待自己的河流。画面里有白板、一句话和围坐的人。

pos.zh: 名词：（写作或研究的）选题

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「多个话题」
加 -al 构成，义为「时事性的；当前相关话题的」

由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「时事性」

senses.title: The subject of a discussion
senses.definition: the subject that a talk, an article, or a meeting is about
senses.definitionCN: 谈话、文章或会议所围绕的主题
senses.example: The speaker changed the topic when the questions became personal.
senses.exampleCN: 问题一涉及私事，讲者就换了话题。
senses.why: The word names the ground the whole exchange stands on, so to change it is to move to different ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指整场交流所立足的那块地，换掉它就是移到另一块地上。

senses.title: A subject for writing
senses.definition: a subject chosen for an essay, a report, or a piece of research
senses.definitionCN: 为论文、报告或研究所选的主题
senses.example: Her topic was the effect of noise on birds in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 她的选题是噪音对城市鸟类的影响。
senses.why: A writer must choose one place among many, and that chosen place is called a topic.
senses.whyCN: 写作者要从许多地方里选出其一，而选定的那一处就叫 topic。

senses.title: A heading in a list
senses.definition: one of the items or headings into which a course or a list is divided
senses.definitionCN: 课程或清单划分出的一个条目
senses.example: The course covers twelve topics, from soil to water quality.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课涵盖十二个主题，从土壤到水质。
senses.why: When a course is divided, each division gets a heading, and each heading inherits the name of a place of argument.
senses.whyCN: 课程被切分时，每一块都有一个标题，而每个标题都继承了「论证所在」这个名字。

senses.title: A subject of public interest
senses.definition: a matter that many people are discussing at present
senses.definitionCN: 当前许多人都在谈论的事情
senses.example: A place becomes crowded when everyone gathers there, so a hot topic is literally a crowded place of talk.
senses.exampleCN: 当所有人聚到一处，那个地方就拥挤起来，所以热门话题字面上是谈话拥挤之地。
senses.why: Once the Greek place word became a subject word, any subject people crowd around could be called hot.
senses.whyCN: 一旦那个希腊「地方」之词变成了「主题」之词，任何众人聚拢的主题都能被称作 hot。

senses.title: A separate matter on the table
senses.definition: one distinct item for decision among several
senses.definitionCN: 若干待决事项中独立的一项
senses.example: Housing is the first topic on the agenda tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 住房是今晚议程上的第一项议题。
senses.why: An agenda is a row of places to visit, and each one is a topic.
senses.whyCN: 议程是一串要依次到访的地点，每一处都是一个 topic。

senses.title: The subject of a study
senses.definition: the central subject around which a study or an investigation is built
senses.definitionCN: 一项研究或调查所围绕的中心主题
senses.example: Choosing a narrow topic makes the reading manageable.
senses.exampleCN: 把主题选窄，阅读量就变得可控。
senses.why: Research needs a single ground that can be covered, so the word means the chosen field of a study.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一块能走完的地面，所以这个词也指一项研究所选定的领域。

senses.title: A conversation opener
senses.definition: a light subject used to begin a conversation
senses.definitionCN: 用来开始交谈的轻松话题
senses.example: Weather is the safest topic with strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 和陌生人聊天，天气是最安全的话题。
senses.why: A safe topic is neutral ground where neither speaker risks an argument.
senses.whyCN: 安全的话题是中立的地面，双方在那儿都不会引发争执。

senses.title: A topic in a text
senses.definition: the subject a passage is organised around, often named in a topic sentence
senses.definitionCN: 一段文字所组织的主题，常由主题句点明
senses.example: The topic of the paragraph is announced in its first sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 这一段的话题由它的第一句点明。
senses.why: A paragraph must announce its ground before building on it, and that announcing sentence takes the name of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一段文字必须先声明它立足的地面，再在其上建构，这个声明句就用了本词之名。

intro.en: Topic comes from the Greek word for place, topika, used of the places of argument in Aristotle's logic; English extended the word from the headings of an argument to any subject.
intro.cn: topic 来自希腊语中表示「地方」的 topika，原指亚里士多德逻辑里论证的「所在」；英语把它从论证的条目扩展到任何主题。

items.en: Topos means a place, and ta topika are the places or common headings from which arguments are drawn.
items.cn: 希腊语 topos 意为地方，ta topika 指抽取论证的「所在」或通用条目。

items.en: Latin topica names the same collection of argument headings, and the word enters learned Latin as a title.
items.cn: 拉丁语 topica 指同一套论证条目，作为书名进入学术拉丁语。

items.en: Old French topic descends from the Latin title and is used of a general heading of thought.
items.cn: 古法语 topic 源自这一拉丁书名，用于表示一般性的思想条目。

items.en: English takes topic in the sixteenth century for a common heading of argument, then for any subject.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 topic，先指论证的常用条目，后指任何主题。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the modern sense of the subject of a talk is ordinary.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，「谈话主题」这一现代义项已很平常。

items.en: Topical and topically grow from it to mean what is currently discussed or locally applied.
items.cn: topical 与 topically 由它派生，意为当前所讨论的，或局部施用的。

note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干的派生词，近义组则汇集表示主题、论点与讨论焦点的词。

core_image: 旧式厨房里，仆人把托盘端得又稳又平
scene: 老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。 The old servant worked for the family for thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里 servant 是「仆人」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。

senses.title: Household worker
senses.definition: a person employed to work in a household
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在家庭中工作的人
senses.example: The old servant worked for the family for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。
senses.why: This is the traditional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是传统义。

senses.title: Public official
senses.definition: a person who works for the state or public
senses.definitionCN: 为国家或公众工作的人
senses.example: Civil servants serve the public.
senses.exampleCN: 公务员为公众服务。
senses.why: Serving expands from a home to a state.
senses.whyCN: 服务从家庭扩展到国家。

senses.title: One who serves
senses.definition: a person who serves a cause or an employer
senses.definitionCN: 为事业或雇主服务的人
senses.example: He was a faithful servant of the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这项事业的忠实服务者。
senses.why: The core idea is service itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心观念是服务本身。

intro.en: Servant comes from Old French servant, from servir, from Latin servire, to serve.
intro.cn: servant 出自古法语 servant，源于 servir，再追溯到拉丁语 servire（服务）。

items.en: Servire meant to serve.
items.cn: servire 意为服务。

items.en: Serviens meant serving.
items.cn: serviens 意为服务的。

items.en: Servant named one who serves.
items.cn: servant 指服务的人。

items.en: English servant named household workers.
items.cn: 英语 servant 指家庭佣人。

items.en: Civil servant names a public official.
items.cn: civil servant 指公务员。

note.en: Servant is compared with similar-looking words and with words for people who serve.
note.cn: 把 servant 与形近词以及表示服务者的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A servant is anyone whose work is to serve, at home or in public office.
normalIntro.cn: servant 是以服务为业的人，无论在家中还是公共岗位。

normal.en: Servant comes from the Latin verb to serve.
normal.cn: servant 出自拉丁语中表示服务的动词。

normal.en: A civil servant works for the state.
normal.cn: 公务员为国家工作。

normal.en: The plural is servants.
normal.cn: 复数形式是 servants。

normal.en: A servant carries out another's orders.
normal.cn: 仆人执行他人的命令。

normal.en: Servant and service share a root.
normal.cn: servant 与 service 同根。

abstract.en: To serve is to put another's need before one's own.
abstract.cn: 服务就是把他人的需要放在自己之前。

abstract.en: The word reminds us who public power belongs to.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们公共权力属于谁。

abstract.en: Dignity belongs to the work, not the title.
abstract.cn: 尊严属于工作本身，而非头衔。

examples.en: The old servant worked for the family for thirty years.
examples.cn: 老仆人为这家人工作了三十年。

examples.en: Civil servants serve the public.
examples.cn: 公务员为公众服务。

examples.en: He was a faithful servant of the cause.
examples.cn: 他是这项事业的忠实服务者。

dict_mnemonic.text: servant 出自古法语 servant，源于拉丁语 servire（服务），本义「服务的人」，后兼指家仆、公务员与事业的服务者。

root: 源自拉丁语 servire（服务），核心义「以服务为业的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Servant means a household worker, a public official, or a person who serves a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: servant 意为仆人、公务员或服务者。

core.en: A person whose role is to serve.
core.cn: 以服务为角色的人。

branches.en: A worker inside a household.
branches.cn: 家庭中的劳动者。

branches.en: A worker inside the state.
branches.cn: 国家机构中的工作者。

branches.en: A person devoted to a cause.
branches.cn: 献身于某项事业的人。

branches.en: Home and state both employ servants.
branches.cn: 家庭与国家都雇用服务者。

branches.en: Public duty and personal devotion meet.
branches.cn: 公共职责与个人忠诚在此相遇。

intro.en: Servant belongs to the Latin servire family of service.
intro.cn: servant 属于拉丁语 servire（服务）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin servire and servus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servire 与 servus 是历史词根。

items.example: The servants kept the house clean.

items.exampleCN: 他奴性的态度让她厌烦。

items.meaning: the state of being a servant

items.exampleCN: 奴性没有为他赢得尊重。

definition_zh: 油；食用油；石油；润滑油；给……上油
definition_en: a thick liquid used for cooking or as fuel, a substance that keeps machinery sliding smoothly, and the verb meaning to put such a liquid on something
core_image: 一只陶罐的罐口挂着油珠，灯光下慢慢往下淌
scene: 厨房的灶台上摆着一只陶罐，罐口挂着金黄的油珠，旁边的铁锅正等着下菜。 She poured a little oil into the hot pan.
sceneCN: 这里的 oil 是「食用油」（第 1 个义项：烹调用的油）；句意为她往热锅里倒了一点油。图中可辨识物件：陶罐、油珠、铁锅。

derivatives.zh: 由 oil 加 -y 构成，义为「油腻的；油状的」
由 oil 加 -er 构成，义为「加油工；油轮」
由 oil 与 field 复合而成，义为「油田」

senses.title: A liquid fat used in cooking
senses.definition: a thick liquid made from plants or animals and used to cook or dress food
senses.definitionCN: 由植物或动物制成、用于烹调或拌食物的黏稠液体
senses.example: The salad was dressed with olive oil and lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 那份沙拉用橄榄油和柠檬调味。
senses.why: The oldest household use of the substance is in food, so the word begins with what sits in the kitchen jar.
senses.whyCN: 这种物质在家庭里最老的用途是入菜，所以这个词的起点就是厨房罐子里的东西。

senses.title: Petroleum extracted from the ground
senses.definition: the dark liquid pumped from beneath the earth and refined into fuel
senses.definitionCN: 从地下抽取、再炼成燃料的深色液体
senses.example: The country's economy depends on oil.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的经济依赖石油。
senses.why: The same substance that fills a kitchen jar also fills pipelines, and industry simply kept the old word for the new scale.
senses.whyCN: 装满厨房罐子的同一种物质也装满管道，工业只是沿用了旧词，去说新的规模。

senses.title: A substance that reduces friction
senses.definition: a prepared liquid put between moving parts so that they slide without wearing
senses.definitionCN: 放在运动部件之间、让它们滑动而不磨损的调制液体
senses.example: The engine needs fresh oil every few thousand miles.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机每跑几千英里就要换新机油。
senses.why: Fat is slippery, so machines borrowed the kitchen word for the stuff that keeps metal from grinding.
senses.whyCN: 油脂是滑的，于是机器借用了厨房里的词，来指让金属不互相摩擦的东西。

senses.title: To put oil on something
senses.definition: to spread or apply oil to a surface, especially to keep it smooth or working
senses.definitionCN: 把油涂到某个表面上，尤指为了让它顺滑或保持运转
senses.example: He oiled the hinges so the gate would stop creaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他给铰链上了油，好让大门不再吱吱响。
senses.why: Once a noun names the substance, the verb can name the act of putting it on, and the object tells you which kind of oil is meant.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指这种物质，动词就能指把油涂上去的动作，而宾语则说明用的是哪一种油。

intro.en: Oil reached English from Old French, which had shortened a Latin word for olive oil; the Greek ancestor of that word is generally taken as the wider source of the family.
intro.cn: oil 经古法语进入英语，而古法语缩短了拉丁语中表示橄榄油的词；一般认为该词的希腊语祖先才是这一族词更早的来源。

items.en: The Greek word elaion named olive oil, and it is generally taken as the source of the wider family of oil words.
items.cn: 希腊语 elaion 指橄榄油，一般认为它是这一族油类词汇更早的来源。

items.en: Latin took the idea as oleum, oil, and kept oliva for the olive itself, so fruit and product had separate names.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 oleum 表示油，同时用 oliva 表示橄榄本身，果实与产物各有名字。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin form to oile and passed it into English speech after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形式缩短为 oile，在诺曼时期之后传入英语口语。

items.en: Middle English oile, later oil, covered cooking fat, lamp fuel and the greasy stuff used on tools.
items.cn: 中古英语的 oile（后作 oil）已兼指食用的油、点灯的油，以及涂在工具上的油脂。

items.en: Modern English extends oil to petroleum, to machine lubricants and to the verb of applying them.
items.cn: 现代英语把 oil 扩展到石油、机器润滑油，以及「涂抹这些油」的动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the oil stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for oily, greasy and fuelling substances.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 oil 词干上的词；近义组收其他表示油性、油脂与燃料物质的名称。

entries.definition: Covered with oil, or tasting and feeling like oil.
entries.definitionCN: 沾满油的，或味道与触感像油的。

entries.definition: A person or device that oils machinery, or a ship carrying oil.
entries.definitionCN: 给机器上油的人或装置，也指运油的船。

entries.definition: An area where petroleum is drilled and pumped.
entries.definitionCN: 开采与抽取石油的区域。

entries.definition: A former name for margarine, built on the Latin word for oil.
entries.definitionCN: 人造黄油旧称，建立在拉丁语「油」一词上。

entries.definition: The mineral oil from which fuels and plastics are made.
entries.definitionCN: 用来制取燃料与塑料的矿物油。

entries.definition: Thick animal fat or a heavy lubricant.
entries.definitionCN: 浓稠的动物脂肪或重型润滑脂。

entries.definition: Any substance that reduces friction between surfaces.
entries.definitionCN: 任何能减少表面之间摩擦的物质。

entries.definition: Material burned to produce heat or power.
entries.definitionCN: 燃烧以产生热量或动力的物质。

normalIntro.en: Oil names the substance before it names any use, and its family grows by describing what is oily, who oils, and where oil is found.
normalIntro.cn: oil 先指这种物质，再指各种用途；词族靠描述「油性的」「上油的人」和「出油的地方」生长。

normal.en: Oil is a short noun with a long history: Greek elaion, Latin oleum, Old French oile, then English oil.
normal.cn: oil 是个短名词，却来历很长：希腊语 elaion、拉丁语 oleum、古法语 oile，再到英语 oil。

normal.en: Oily is oil plus -y, the suffix that turns a substance into a quality.
normal.cn: oily 是 oil 加 -y，这个后缀把一种物质变成一种性质。

normal.en: Oiler adds -er, so it names the person or device that does the oiling.
normal.cn: oiler 加 -er，因此指上油的人或装置。

normal.en: Oilfield is a compound: the field is where the oil is, not what it is made of.
normal.cn: oilfield 是复合词：field 指油所在的地方，而不是油由什么做成。

normal.en: The verb oil keeps the same shape, so oiled hinges and oiling a gate show the act without a new spelling.
normal.cn: 动词 oil 形态不变，所以 oiled hinges 与 oiling a gate 直接用原形加词尾表示动作。

abstract.en: One word for food, fuel and lubricant suggests that what matters is the slipperiness, not the purpose.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指食物、燃料与润滑剂，说明关键在「滑」，而不在用途。

abstract.en: Oil is ancient sunlight stored in liquid, which is why the same word can feed a kitchen and drive a nation.
abstract.cn: 石油是储存在液体里的远古阳光，所以同一个词既能养一间厨房，也能驱动一个国家。

abstract.en: To oil something is to make the world move more quietly, one hinge at a time.
abstract.cn: 给东西上油，就是让世界更安静地转动，一次一个铰链。

examples.en: A drop of oil fell from the jar onto the table.
examples.cn: 一滴油从罐子落到桌上。

examples.en: The truck carries crude oil from the port each night.
examples.cn: 卡车每晚从港口运走原油。

examples.en: He oiled the gate before the winter rains came.
examples.cn: 冬雨来临前他给大门上了油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「熬油」——小火慢熬，油才出来；记住 oil 是油。

root: 来自古法语 oile，再上溯拉丁语 oleum（油），一般认为更早与希腊语 elaion（橄榄油）相关；同一词干也给出 oliva（橄榄）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a thick slippery liquid; cooking, petroleum, lubrication and the act of applying it are four directions that liquid goes.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种黏稠而滑的液体；入菜、石油、润滑以及涂抹动作，是这种液体走出的四个方向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clay jar with a bead of oil hanging at its mouth, slowly running down in the lamplight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只陶罐的罐口挂着油珠，灯光下慢慢往下淌。

branches.en: a jar of golden oil beside a hot pan
branches.cn: 热锅旁一罐金黄的油

branches.en: a pipeline crossing dry ground at night
branches.cn: 夜里穿过旱地的输油管

branches.en: a drop of oil placed between two gears
branches.cn: 滴在两个齿轮之间的一滴油

branches.en: a hand oiling a gate hinge before winter
branches.cn: 入冬前给门铰链上油的手

branches.en: the same slippery stuff moving from kitchen to machine
branches.cn: 同一种滑腻之物，从厨房移到机器

intro.en: The word comes from a Greek and Latin noun for olive oil, shortened by French and then fitted with English endings that name a quality and a worker.
intro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语与拉丁语中表示橄榄油的名词，经法语缩短，再接上英语词尾，用来指一种性质和一个干活的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin oleum, oliva and oleosus are recorded, so the English family has a reliable Latin ancestry even though the earliest form is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oleum、oliva、oleosus 均有记录，所以尽管最早的形式来自希腊语，这一族英语词仍有可靠的拉丁语世系。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 兴趣；利益；利息；v. 使感兴趣
definition_en: the feeling of wanting to know more about something, an advantage you gain, or money paid for the use of money
core_image: 一个人把头探过桌边，眼睛跟着别人手里的书页一起移动
scene: 少年挤在人群外圈，踮着脚看摊主手上的老式钟表，舍不得走。 The bank pays a little interest on that account each month.
sceneCN: 这里 interest 是「兴趣」（第 1 个义项：想知道更多的心情），句意银行每月给那个账户付一点利息，用的是第 2 个义项。画面里的物件：老式钟表、踮起的脚、存折。

pos.zh: 名词：兴趣；利益；利息；股份
动词：使感兴趣；引起（某人）注意

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「有趣的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「感兴趣的」
由 interesting 加 -ly 构成，义为「有趣的是」
由否定前缀 dis- 加过去分词构成，义为「不带私利的」

senses.title: Wanting to know more
senses.definition: a feeling of curiosity or attention that makes you want to know more about something
senses.definitionCN: 一种好奇或注意的心情，使你想对某事了解更多
senses.example: His interest in old watches began at a street market.
senses.exampleCN: 他对旧钟表的兴趣始于一个街头小市集。
senses.why: Latin interest means "it is between", that is, it makes a difference to someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 interest 意为「它在其间」，即与人有关、对人有差别。

senses.title: Money paid for money
senses.definition: the money that a borrower pays to a lender for the use of the money over time
senses.definitionCN: 借用人因使用这笔钱而按时间付给放款人的钱
senses.example: A small loan at seven per cent interest adds up quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之七利率的小额贷款很快就滚出不少钱。
senses.why: Roman law made it profitable to have a stake in a loan, and interest came to mean that stake.
senses.whyCN: 罗马法使在借贷中占一份成为有利可图之事，interest 遂指这「一份」。

senses.title: What is good for you
senses.definition: the advantage or benefit of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体的好处与得益
senses.example: The road was closed in the interest of safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路为了安全而被封闭。
senses.why: What makes a difference to you is also what serves your advantage.
senses.whyCN: 对你有差别的事，也就是对你有利的事。

senses.title: A share in a business
senses.definition: a legal share or stake in a company or property
senses.definitionCN: 在公司或财产中的合法份额
senses.example: She sold her interest in the shop to her partner.
senses.exampleCN: 她把店里的股份卖给了合伙人。
senses.why: From a stake in a loan the word widened to any ownership share.
senses.whyCN: 从借贷中的一份，此词扩展到任何所有权份额。

senses.title: To draw attention
senses.definition: to make someone want to know or take part
senses.definitionCN: 使某人想了解或参与
senses.example: The teacher interested the class in the old maps on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 老师让全班对墙上的旧地图产生了兴趣。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: it plants the curiosity instead of feeling it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词反过来用：不是产生好奇，而是种下好奇。

intro.en: Interest began as the Latin verb phrase interest "it makes a difference", from inter and esse "to be".
intro.cn: interest 起初是拉丁语动词短语 interest「与之有关」，由 inter 与 esse「存在」构成。

items.en: Interest is literally "it is between", used in phrases like interest reipublicae, it matters to the state.
items.cn: interest 字面是「它在中间」，见于 interest reipublicae 等短语，意谓对国家有干系。

items.en: Roman law compensated a lender for the delay in repayment, weighing what it mattered to him.
items.cn: 罗马法就延迟还款补偿放款人，衡量的正是此事对他有多大干系。

items.en: French interest narrowed to mean money paid for the use of money.
items.cn: 法语 interest 窄化为为使用金钱而付的钱。

items.en: English took interest in the sixteenth century for both money and advantage.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 interest，兼指利息与好处。

items.en: The sense of curiosity appeared later and became the commonest use of all.
items.cn: 「好奇」这一义项较晚出现，却成了最常见用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb esse "to be"; the near-meaning group holds other words for attention and money.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语动词 esse「存在」；近义组收表示注意与钱财的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for things that hold attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容能吸引注意的事物。

entries.definition: The adjective for the person who feels interest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容感到兴趣的人。

entries.definition: Free from personal gain, not merely bored.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无利害关系的」，并非「不感兴趣」。

entries.definition: The wish to know, without any stake.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「好奇心」，不带利益。

entries.definition: An advantage, especially as a right.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「益处」，尤指应得的权利。

entries.definition: Money made from a business after costs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「利润」，扣除成本后的所赚。

normalIntro.en: The hooks run from the phrase "it matters to me" to the exact phrases interest lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从「这事与我有关」一路走到 interest 的真实搭配。

normal.en: Interest first meant "it is between": it stands between a person and a thing.
normal.cn: interest 最早意为「在其中间」：站在人与事物之间。

normal.en: Be interested in a topic, take an interest in a hobby.
normal.cn: 对话题用 be interested in，对爱好用 take an interest in。

normal.en: Interest on a loan is your stake in the lender's delay.
normal.cn: 贷款的利息就是你对放款人拖延所占的那一份。

normal.en: In the interest of safety, the road was closed.
normal.cn: 为了安全，这条路被封闭。

normal.en: A conflict of interest means two gains pull against each other.
normal.cn: 利益冲突指的是两份好处互相拉扯。

abstract.en: Interest is the thread that ties attention to advantage.
abstract.cn: 兴趣是把注意力与好处系在一起的那根线。

abstract.en: Money grows by interest; the mind grows by interest too.
abstract.cn: 钱靠利息增长，心也靠兴趣增长。

abstract.en: What matters to you will always hold your eyes.
abstract.cn: 与你有关的事总会牵住你的眼睛。

examples.en: Her interest in birds began with a single nest outside the window.
examples.cn: 她对鸟的兴趣始于窗外的一个鸟巢。

examples.en: The loan is repaid with interest over five years.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款在五年内连本带息还清。

examples.en: He acted in the interest of the whole village, not himself.
examples.cn: 他是为整个村子而非自己行事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因戳瑞斯特」——因被戳到痒处，立刻来了兴趣

root: 拉丁语 inter「在……之间」+ esse「存在」→ 动词短语 interest「与之有关」→ 古法语 interest → 英语 interest。同族：interesting、interested。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: curiosity, money for money, advantage, a share in a business, and the verb of arousing curiosity.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：好奇、钱生钱的利息、好处、生意里的份额，以及使人上心的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person leaning forward, eyes following someone else's book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人探身向前，眼睛跟着别人手里的书走。

branches.en: THE MARKET STALL: curiosity makes the boy stop walking.
branches.cn: 小摊这条线：好奇心让少年停住脚。

branches.en: THE SAVINGS BOOK: money earns money over time.
branches.cn: 存折这条线：钱随时间再生钱。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ROAD: a benefit is weighed against a cost.
branches.cn: 封闭的路这条线：好处要与代价权衡。

branches.en: THE SOLD SHARE: ownership is the same stake in property.
branches.cn: 卖出的股份这条线：所有权即财产中的一份。

branches.en: THE OLD MAPS: a teacher plants the curiosity.
branches.cn: 旧地图这条线：老师把好奇种下去。

intro.en: Interest has no living prefix-and-suffix split in English: it is frozen Latin, inter "between" plus the verb "to be".
intro.cn: interest 在英语里已无活的词缀可分，是一块冻结的拉丁语：inter「在……之间」加「存在」动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin interest and the phrase interest reipublicae are recorded; only the deepest IE layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interest 与短语 interest reipublicae 均有记载，只有最深的印欧层是重构。

items.example: It places the matter among people.
items.exampleCN: 它把这件事安放在人与人之间。

items.example: The verb behind est and interest.
items.exampleCN: est 与 interest 背后的动词。
